escena: SCENE (colour review, post studio in Bogota, evening): a SPLIT-DIOPTER shot — two planes at very different distances are BOTH perfectly sharp at the same time, which no normal lens can do. Verify it by these landmarks: in the near LEFT of the frame, the corner of a printed proof held close to the lens is razor sharp down to its paper grain and its CYAN halftone fields, and it occupies the left third; on the RIGHT, he is seen from the CHEST UP ONLY — his head and shoulders fill the right two thirds of the frame, close to the camera, no waist, no arms, no desk in front of him — and he is ALSO razor sharp, down to the thin silver top bar of his glasses and the individual hairs of his long beard; between the two planes there is a soft vertical seam where the two fields of focus meet, a strip visibly softer than both. A large AZURE-BLUE calibration screen showing a FLAT EVEN BLUE FIELD, no photograph on it, fills the wall behind him and is the only light on his face, so a cool blue rim edges his cheek, the frame of his glasses and his shoulder; a single hard desk lamp rakes across the proof from the left. Resting on the console in the near plane, an ORANGE grease pencil is the only warm object in the picture, no more than three percent of the frame. Caught at the instant he lowers his chin, agreeing with what is on the proof. He wears a faded olive linen shirt; no navy or blue clothing. He looks at the proof, never at the camera. 85mm, close. Everything is completely unbranded, no readable text anywhere.

lecho.objeto: the near edge of the console in shadow at the bottom of the frame
lecho.tono: DARK near black in shadow, matte
